rationale: No supported optimization is safe to apply. The run-test-matrix job already benefits from GitHub Actions' default fail-fast behavior (default: true), so explicitly setting fail-fast: true would be a no-op and the P-LIT-FAIL-FAST evidence is synthetic with unmeasured savings. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT has measured evidence (26.8% elapsed savings on a fork) but its precondition requires representative successful-duration history, and this repository reports no completed runs / no measured baseline; moreover the matrix builds C/C++ with sanitizers and runs large_insert_stress_tests/perf_tests, so a short fixed timeout risks violating the contraindication that valid slow runs exceed the limit and would reduce test coverage. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is already addressed by the existing awalsh128/cache-apt-pkgs-action usage for apt dependencies, and adding another cache would be an unrelated change without a measured lockfile/environment input. Change-filtering, stale-run cancellation, and schedule-based patterns either require new actions/network access, could skip required checks on PRs, or lack applicable triggers (workflow only runs on pull_request).
